officialTitle: Atezolizumab versus docetaxel in patients with previously treated non-small-cell lung cancer (OAK): a phase 3, open-label, multicentre randomised controlled trial

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: The primary efficacy analysis was done in the first 850 of 1225 enrolled patients.

sponsor: F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd, Genentech, Inc.
clinicalQuestion: Does atezolizumab improve overall survival over docetaxel in previously treated advanced NSCLC, irrespective of PD-L1 expression?

pico.population: Stage IIIB/IV squamous or non-squamous NSCLC after one to two prior cytotoxic regimens (≥1 platinum-based), ECOG PS 0–1
pico.outcomes: Co-primary: OS in ITT and in PD-L1 TC1/2/3 or IC1/2/3. Safety

arms.label: Atezolizumab
arms.doseSourceQuote: to intravenously receive either atezolizumab 1200 mg or docetaxel 75 mg/mevery 3 weeks

arms.label: Docetaxel
arms.doseSourceQuote: to intravenously receive either atezolizumab 1200 mg or docetaxel 75 mg/mevery 3 weeks

publications.title: Atezolizumab versus docetaxel in patients with previously treated non-small-cell lung cancer (OAK): a phase 3, open-label, multicentre randomised controlled trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: In the ITT population, overall survival was improved with atezolizumab compared with docetaxel (median overall survival was 13·8 months [95% CI 11·8-15·7] vs 9·6 months [8·6-11·2]; hazard ratio [HR] 0·73 [95% CI 0·62-0·87], p=0·0003).

Overall survival in the TC1/2/3 or IC1/2/3 population was improved with atezolizumab (n=241) compared with docetaxel (n=222; median overall survival was 15·7 months [95% CI 12·6-18·0] with atezolizumab vs 10·3 months [8·8-12·0] with docetaxel; HR 0·74 [95% CI 0·58-0·93]; p=0·0102).
Patients in the PD-L1 low or undetectable subgroup (TC0 and IC0) also had improved survival with atezolizumab (median overall survival 12·6 months vs 8·9 months; HR 0·75 [95% CI 0·59-0·96]).

safety.sourceQuote: Fewer patients had treatment-related grade 3 or 4 adverse events with atezolizumab (90 [15%] of 609 patients) versus docetaxel (247 [43%] of 578 patients).

strengths: Randomised phase III with OS co-primary endpoints
OS benefit regardless of PD-L1 expression or histology

clinicalImplications.text: Established atezolizumab over docetaxel in previously treated advanced NSCLC irrespective of PD-L1 status or histology.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Even PD-L1 TC0/IC0 tumours derived OS benefit from second-line atezolizumab versus docetaxel in OAK.
